title: Junior Core Mathematics • Objective Mastery Series (Set 43)
subject: Mathematics

questions.prompt: If set $$A = \{2, 3, 5, 9, 12\}$$ and set $$B = \{9, 2, k, 5, 3\}$$ such that $$A = B$$, what is the value of $k$?
questions.hint: Equal sets contain the exact same elements.
questions.workedSolution: Comparing the elements of A and B, the missing element in B is 12. Therefore, k = 12.

questions.prompt: Given sets $$P = \{\text{car}, \text{bus}\}$$ and $$Q = \{\text{van}, \text{car}, \text{bus}\}$$, which of the following statements is TRUE?
questions.hint: All elements of set P are also contained in set Q.
questions.workedSolution: Since every member of P is also an element of Q and P does not equal Q, P is a proper subset of Q ($$P \subset Q$$).

questions.prompt:
The following vertical addition is performed in base ten:
$$\begin{matrix} 3240 \\ + 1150 \\ + x \\ \hline 6150 \end{matrix}$$
Find the missing addend $x$.
questions.hint: Add the first two numbers: $3240 + 1150 = 4390$. Subtract from 6150.

questions.prompt: Given that $$3^2 \times 2^2 \times 5 = 180$$, find the least positive integer that must be multiplied by $180$ to make the product a perfect square.
questions.hint: For a number to be a perfect square, all exponents in its prime factorization must be even.
questions.workedSolution: The factor 5 has an exponent of 1. Multiplying by 5 gives $$3^2 \times 2^2 \times 5^2 = (3 \times 2 \times 5)^2 = 30^2$$.

questions.prompt: Express $5384.15$ in standard form.
questions.hint: Move the decimal point 3 places to the left so that $1 \le A < 10$.

questions.prompt: Convert the binary numeral $$11011_{\text{two}}$$ to a decimal numeral (base ten).
A student spent $3/8$ of her pocket money on books and $1/4$ on lunch. What fraction of her pocket money was spent altogether on books and lunch?
questions.hint: Add the fractions: $\frac{3}{8} + \frac{1}{4}$.

questions.prompt: The product of three numbers is $1,560$. Two of the numbers are $4$ and $13$. Find the third number.
questions.hint: Product of the first two = $4 \times 13 = 52$. Divide 1,560 by 52.

questions.prompt: Find the Greatest Common Factor (GCF) of $$2^4 \times 3^2$$ and $$2^2 \times 3^3$$.
questions.hint: Take the lowest power of each common prime factor: $2^2 \times 3^2$.

questions.prompt: Two supplementary interior angles on the same side of a transversal crossing two parallel lines are in the ratio $2 : 3$. Find the size of the larger angle.
questions.hint: Co-interior angles sum to 180°. Larger angle = (3 / 5) × 180°.

questions.prompt: From Question 10, find the size of the smaller interior angle.
questions.hint: Subtract: 180° - 108°.

questions.prompt: If an angle is vertically opposite to an angle measuring $72^\circ$, what is its measure?
questions.hint: Vertically opposite angles are equal.
questions.workedSolution: Vertically opposite angles have equal measure, so the angle is $$72^\circ$$.

questions.prompt: Simplify: $$4x^2 y^3 \times 3x^3 y$$.
questions.hint: Multiply coefficients: $4 \times 3 = 12$. Add exponents for x and y.

questions.prompt: In the relation $$v = u + at$$, find $v$ when $u = 8$, $a = 5$, and $t = 3$.
questions.hint: Substitute the values: $8 + (5 \times 3)$.

questions.prompt: The test scores of ten students are: $$2, 3, 4, 4, 6, 8, 8, 8, 9, 10$$. What is the modal score?
questions.hint: The mode is the score occurring with the highest frequency.
questions.workedSolution: Score 8 appears 3 times, which is more frequent than any other score. Mode = 8.

questions.prompt: From the test scores in Question 15 ($$2, 3, 4, 4, 6, 8, 8, 8, 9, 10$$), find the median score.
questions.hint: The middle two values (5th and 6th) are 6 and 8. Average them.

questions.prompt: Calculate the mean of the ten scores in Question 15 ($$2, 3, 4, 4, 6, 8, 8, 8, 9, 10$$).
questions.hint: Sum all scores and divide by 10.

questions.prompt: What is the probability of selecting a student who scored $8$ from the group in Question 15?
questions.hint: Score 8 appears 3 times out of 10 students.

questions.prompt: A real estate agent earns a commission of $10\%$ on property sales. If his commission on a house sale is $\text{GH¢ } 45,000.00$, find the total sale price of the house.
questions.hint: Total sales = Commission / 0.10.

questions.prompt: A map is drawn to a scale of $1 : 50,000$. What actual distance in kilometres is represented by a segment of $6\text{ cm}$ on the map?
questions.hint: $$6\text{ cm} \times 50,000 = 300,000\text{ cm}$$. Divide by 100,000 to convert to kilometres.

questions.prompt: Kofi and Ama share an amount of $\text{GH¢ } 800.00$ in the ratio $5 : 3$. Find Kofi's share.
questions.hint: Total ratio parts = 5 + 3 = 8. Kofi's share = (5 / 8) × 800.

questions.prompt: Simplify: $$\frac{3x}{4} - \frac{x - y}{2}$$.
questions.hint: Common denominator is 4: $\frac{3x - 2(x - y)}{4}$.

questions.prompt: If $$y^7 \div y^4 = 27$$, find the value of $y$.
Find one-hundredth ($1/100$) of $2.485$.
questions.hint: Dividing by 100 shifts the decimal point 2 places to the left.

questions.prompt: State the rule for the linear mapping where inputs $x = \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ produce outputs $y = \{3, 5, 7, 9\}$.
questions.hint: Common difference is 2. At $x = 1$, $2(1) + 1 = 3$.
questions.workedSolution: Rate of change is 2 ($2x$). When $x = 1$, $2(1) + c = 3 \implies c = 1$. The rule is $$x \to 2x + 1$$.

questions.prompt: The circumference of a circular running track is $880\text{ m}$. Find the diameter of the track. (Take $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$).
questions.hint: Circumference $C = \pi d \implies d = \frac{C}{\pi}$.

questions.prompt: Given column vectors $$u = \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \end{pmatrix}$$ and $$v = \begin{pmatrix} -1 \\ 2 \end{pmatrix}$$, evaluate $$3(u + v)$$.
questions.hint: $$u + v = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 5 \end{pmatrix}$$. Multiply each component by 3.

questions.prompt: Which of the following geometric instruments is primarily used to measure the size of an angle in degrees?
questions.hint: Standard semi-circular graduated angle-measuring tool.
questions.workedSolution: A protractor is specifically designed for measuring and constructing angles in degrees.

questions.prompt: Express the ratio of $75\text{ cm}$ to $50\text{ cm}$ in its simplest form.
questions.hint: Divide both numbers by their highest common factor, 25.

questions.prompt: A line segment of length $4\text{ cm}$ is enlarged to a new length of $12\text{ cm}$. What is the linear scale factor of enlargement?
questions.hint: Scale factor = Image length / Object length.

questions.prompt: If a line segment of length $5.4\text{ m}$ is enlarged by a scale factor of $1/3$, find the length of the image segment.
questions.hint: Multiply 5.4 by 1/3.

questions.prompt: In a right-angled triangle $PQR$, right-angled at $Q$, side $|PQ| = 12\text{ cm}$ and side $|QR| = 5\text{ cm}$. Find the value of $\tan \angle PRQ$.
questions.hint: $\tan \theta = \text{Opposite} / \text{Adjacent}$. Opposite side to angle R is PQ = 12.

questions.prompt: A customer purchased a gas stove for $\text{GH¢ } 360.00$ after receiving a $10\%$ cash discount on the marked price. Calculate the marked price.
questions.hint: Customer paid 90% of the marked price: Marked Price = 360.00 / 0.90.

questions.prompt: In a class of $45$ pupils, $25$ study French, $7$ study both French and Spanish, and each pupil studies at least one of the two languages. How many pupils study Spanish?
questions.hint: $$n(F \cup S) = n(F) + n(S) - n(F \cap S) \implies 45 = 25 + n(S) - 7$$.

questions.prompt: From Question 34, how many pupils study Spanish ONLY?
questions.hint: Spanish only = Total Spanish - Both = 27 - 7.

questions.prompt: From Question 34, how many pupils study French ONLY?
questions.hint: French only = Total French - Both = 25 - 7.

questions.prompt: When a certain number is subtracted from $14$ and the difference is multiplied by $3$, the result is $18$. Find the number.
Point $B$ is located on a three-figure bearing of $045^\circ$ from Point $A$. What is the bearing of $A$ from $B$?
questions.hint: Back-bearing = Forward bearing $+ 180^\circ$ when $< 180^\circ$.

questions.prompt: If $24\%$ of the length of a cord is $72\text{ cm}$, find the full length of the cord.
questions.hint: Full length = $72 / 0.24$.

questions.prompt: In a geometric compass construction, intersecting arcs centered at points on a line equidistant from an external point $P$ are used to:
options: Construct a perpendicular to a given line from a point outside the line
Construct a line parallel to the given line
questions.correctAnswer: Construct a perpendicular to a given line from a point outside the line
questions.hint: The construction drops a perpendicular line onto a line segment from an external point.
questions.workedSolution: This standard compass technique constructs a perpendicular from an external point onto a given straight line.
